patch.value: GH-931: linked-test detector misclassifies unrelated node dist/cli.js commands as pm
The linked-test execution classifier treats any Node script ending in dist/cli.js as the pm CLI, so unrelated project commands receive false PM context, mismatch, and sandbox diagnostics.

PM command detection proves executable identity instead of matching a generic dist/cli.js suffix; actual pm binary package and checkout invocations remain recognized; unrelated Node CLIs remain non-PM with and without leading environment assignments; execution-context and mismatch receipts stay accurate across CLI and SDK tests.
@unbrained/pm-cli 2026.8.7 linked-test runner in a non-pm consuming project

Link node dist/cli.js schema research --format json with pm test --add-json, run pm test ITEM --run, and observe execution_context.is_pm_command=true plus mismatch_detected=true for the unrelated executable; repeat with a leading environment assignment.
Only an executable whose pm identity is established receives PM execution context; generic project dist/cli.js commands remain ordinary linked tests.
The 2026.8.7 suffix heuristic marks every node path ending in dist/cli.js as pm and emits false mismatch metadata.
Ordinary project tests are mislabeled and can be failed or rerouted by PM context enforcement, undermining the trustworthiness of linked verification evidence.
